source.title: Trajeglish: Learning the Language of Driving Scenarios
source.authors: Jonah Philion; X. Peng; S. Fidler

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a preliminary scaling study of a motion-token model, extending loss-scaling investigation to a non-text setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling results in Figure 11. The nuScenes transfer comparison and benchmark results are not rows because they do not test a loss-scaling relationship. The paper does not fit or report power-law exponents.
record.test_reason: Figure 11 reports validation loss for a motion-token transformer across dataset sizes (about 1e7 to 1e9 tokens) for two parameter counts. This is a new, non-text setting bearing on V5. However, it uses only two model sizes, fits no power law and reports no exponents, so it cannot establish whether the power-law form holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors call the scaling study preliminary and say Trajeglish is severely data-constrained on WOMD compared with LLMs. The 15.4M and 35.6M models are equivalent up to 0.5B tokens, and the authors infer large gains if data grew beyond WOMD's roughly 1B tokens. They defer more extensive scaling studies to future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an autoregressive motion-token model and validation loss on WOMD, rather than the original language-model scaling setup; it reports a preliminary sweep without fitting power laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported parameter-count gains depend on dataset size: the two model sizes are described as equivalent up to 0.5B tokens, with the larger model just beginning to outperform at WOMD-scale data.
record.problems: The scaling analysis is explicitly preliminary; numerical values are available only as plotted curves, no power-law fits or exponents are reported, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.

untested.parts: Whether loss follows a power law at all in motion-token modeling: no fit, no exponents, only two model sizes and no compute sweep. Image/video models, repeated data, and scaling under fine-tuning or transfer are also untested; the nuScenes transfer has no scale sweep.
Not tested: this is not a language model.
Not tested: no extrapolation from small runs.
Not tested: downstream metrics are not related to scale.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict is given. The only evidence is two loss-versus-data curves with no fitted form. Loss decreasing with data is compatible with V5, but it does not show a power law. The parameter-size gap appearing only at large data matches the data-bottleneck caveat in V1/V5, so it does not limit their scope. The reader's limits_scope label is therefore dropped. The nuScenes fine-tuning curves (Fig. 12) compare training strategies, not scaling, and are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
No prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted to small runs.
No compute-budget sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Only motion-token modeling on WOMD is examined for scaling; the study does not test image or video models, repeated data, or scaling under fine-tuning and transfer.
No relationship between pretraining loss and downstream task performance is measured.
No fitting-method comparison, exponent comparison, or test of curves bending away from a fitted power law.

rows.subject: Trajeglish, 15.4M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate validation loss across dataset sizes.
rows.locator: Figure 11, left panel; Section 4.3, Preliminary Scaling Law
rows.note: The text says this model's performance is equivalent to the 35.6M-parameter model up to 0.5B tokens. Numerical loss values and a fitted functional form are not reported.
rows.check: The measure is vehicle validation loss only (Fig. 11 y-axis). The plot shows loss falling as dataset size grows on a log axis, roughly 0.58 to 0.52 read off the figure. No fit is reported, so the power-law form cannot be checked. The row should state the vehicle-only measure and the approximate 1e7–1e9 token range.

rows.subject: Trajeglish, 35.6M parameters
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate validation loss across dataset sizes.
rows.baseline: 15.4M-parameter model; text says performance is equivalent up to 0.5B tokens
rows.locator: Figure 11, left panel; Section 4.3, Preliminary Scaling Law
rows.note: The authors state that this model is only just significantly better for datasets the size of WOMD; the paper gives no numerical loss values or power-law fit.
rows.check: The 35.6M model matches the 15.4M model up to 0.5B tokens and is only just better at WOMD size (about 1.5B tokens). V1/V5 expect little parameter gain when data is the bottleneck, so this is not a weaker-than-claimed effect. With only two sizes, no parameter-scaling form can be read, so 'partial' overstates the evidence. The baseline is the 15.4M model's curve.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
